thread:
olivia: Heads-up: p95 token latency for ap-south routes spiked around 10:12 UTC. Looks tied to an abrupt routing shift and several kernel fallbacks. anyone oncall?

sam: saw it too. route=ap-south-chat p95 50ms -> 320ms. routing logs show failover to eu-west at 10:11:59.

monitor-bot: [ALERT] route.token.p95(ap-south-chat) > 200ms (1m) at 10:12:06 UTC

olivia: quick capture from a worker that saw the slow tail:
```
[10:11:58] autoscaler: reclaimed node ap-south-2 (drain)
[10:11:59] kernel_select: preferred=attn-opt-fast, selected=attn-compat, reason=workspace_fragmentation
[10:12:00] batcher: effective_batch=3 target_batch=12 (preempted)
[10:12:00] kvcache: evictions=120, miss_rate=0.46
[10:12:01] routing: decision=failover dst=eu-west-3
```

houston: workspace_fragmentation + high kvcache miss_rate = bad combo. which phase accounts for most of the added latency?

olivia: pulled phase-labelled histograms. PromQL snippets I used:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,route,phase))
sum by(route,phase) (rate(token_latency_count[5m]))
```
phase ∈ {tokenize, kv_lookup, kv_deserialize, attn_exec, kernel_launch, io}

sam: suggestion for dashboard updates:
- waterfall panel: stacked p50/p95/p99 by phase per route (dropdown)
- overlay lines: kvcache.miss_rate and routing.failover_rate
- kernel_fallback timeline: selected_kernel by node with reasons
- cross-region RTT heatmap: probe_rtt_millis{src_region=~"ap-.*",dst_region=~"eu-.*"}

houston: let's add a derived "kernel_headroom_pct" metric: (gpu_total_bytes - workspace_used_bytes - gpu_reserved_bytes) / gpu_total_bytes * 100. expose as per-node gauge and add alert.

olivia: I'll add kernel_headroom_pct gauge to the node exporter and wire it to Grafana. PromQL draft:
```
avg by(node) ((node_gpu_total_bytes - node_workspace_used_bytes - node_gpu_reserved_bytes) / node_gpu_total_bytes) * 100
```

sam: alerting proposals:
- route.token.p95 > 200ms for 2m -> page oncall
- kvcache.miss_rate > 0.25 for 1m -> ops (no page)
- kernel_fallback_rate(reason=workspace_fragmentation) > 0.08 for 5m -> eng-runtime
- kernel_headroom_pct < 12% for any node for 3m -> infra

houston: autoscaler note: it reclaimed nodes quickly which likely triggered fragmentation and cache eviction. infra, can we prefer whole-node reclaim vs shaving across many nodes when fragmentation risk is high?

infra-bot: [AUTOSCALER] ap-south/reserved-pool scaled from 10 -> 4 at 10:11:57 (policy: reclaim)

olivia: runtime mitigation idea: memory-aware kernel selection scoring. if kernel_headroom_pct low or fragmentation high, prefer kernels with smaller contiguous workspace even if slightly higher per-op latency. also, if kvcache.miss_rate spikes, prefer routing to warm pools in-region before cross-region failover.

sam: ops-side: add an autoscaler annotation stream in Grafana (deploy/autoscaler/infra-bot messages) so we can correlate spikes with scale events.

houston: quick runbook steps for this class of alert:
1) check kernel_fallback_rate and kernel_headroom_pct around alert time
2) check autoscaler events and nodes drained
3) check kvcache.miss_rate and consider temporary route override to warm pool in-region
4) if reproducible, capture nvtx or lightweight CUDA timeline during repro to see per-token kernel overhead

olivia: action items:
- olivia: add waterfall panel + kvcache and failover overlays (EOD)
- olivia: instrument kernel_headroom_pct metric and dashboard gauge (tomorrow)
- infra: PR to prefer whole-node reclaim when fragmentation risk high (in review)
- eng-runtime: prototype memory-aware kernel selection scoring (WIP)
- sam: schedule nvtx trace run in ap-south-staging at 15:00 UTC and attach timeline

monitor-bot: [NOTE] incident logged: INCIDENT-2026-03-ap-south-kv-kernel-fallback

houston: tl;dr: aggressive reclaim caused fragmentation and KV evictions -> kernel fallbacks -> cross-region failover -> token p95 spike. Dashboards, kernel_headroom alerts, autoscaler gating, and kernel scoring are the main mitigations.
